etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English cameraman.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English garage (given the transcribed form, perhaps borrowed from British English garage), from French garage. Doublet of グラージ.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English catch.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English group.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Blend of ジーンズ (jīnzu, “jeans”) + パンツ (pantsu, “pants”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From English timer.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English no.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English bar. Doublet of バール and バル.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English pattern.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English free.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the spelling pronunciation of English buzzer.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English bed.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English boycott.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 世 is a daiyōji replacing 輿.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Uncertain.
May be from written Chinese 冒頭 /冒头 (màotóu), analyzable as 冒 (“to emerge”) + 頭 (“the head; the top; the beginning”).
First attested in the 1880s in Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 助(たす)ける (tasukeru, “to help, to aid, to assist”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from verb 報(ほう)ずる (hōzuru), by natural progression from サ行変格活用 (sa-gyō henkaku katsuyō, “s-irregular conjugation”) verbs ending in -uru to 上一段活用 (kami ichidan katsuyō, “upper monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -iru.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 大 (ō-, “large”) + 空 (sora, “sky”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 天體 (MC then thejX). Analyzable as
天 (ten, “heaven”) + 体 (tai, “body”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Old Japanese, from Proto-Japonic *pisǝka.https://starlingdb.org/cgi-bin/response.cgi?root=config&morpho=0&basename=\data\alt\japet&first=1101

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Originally a compound of 身(み) (mi, “body”) + 木(き) (ki, “tree”).
First cited to a text from 1726.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 戀愛 (MC ljwenH 'ojH).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese compound 手法 (MC syuwX pjop). Compare modern Mandarin 手法 (shǒufǎ).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 救(すく)う (sukuu, “to save”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 漢語 (MC xanH ngjoX, “Han, Chinese + speech, language”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 痛 (tsū, "severe, "vehement," "keen") + 切 (setsu, "keen," "acute," "intense").

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 棄 is a daiyōji replacing 毀.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 素 (そ, so: “element”) + 材 (ざい, zai: “material”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 詫(わ)びる (wabiru, “to apologise”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
⟨mi₁yako₁⟩ → */mʲijakʷo/ → /mijako/
From Old Japanese, a compound of 宮(みや) (miya, “imperial palace”) + 処(こ) (ko, “place”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 都 (MC tu).
